source.name: sp_UpsertProducts
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_UpsertProducts
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    BEGIN TRANSACTION;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Update existing products
    -------------------------------------------------
    UPDATE p
    SET
        ProductName = s.ProductName,
        Price = s.Price,
        StockQuantity = s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.Products p
    INNER JOIN dbo.ProductImportStaging s
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Insert new products
    -------------------------------------------------
    INSERT INTO dbo.Products
    (
        ProductName,
        SKU,
        Price,
        StockQuantity
    )
    SELECT
        s.ProductName,
        s.SKU,
        s.Price,
        s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Products p
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Delete removed products
    -------------------------------------------------
    DELETE p
    FROM dbo.Products p
    LEFT JOIN dbo.ProductImportStaging s
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE s.SKU IS NULL;

    COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END;

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_UpsertProducts()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Update existing products
    -------------------------------------------------
    UPDATE dbo.Products p
    SET
        ProductName = s.ProductName,
        Price = s.Price,
        StockQuantity = s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    WHERE p.SKU = s.SKU;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Insert new products
    -------------------------------------------------
    INSERT INTO dbo.Products
    (
        ProductName,
        SKU,
        Price,
        StockQuantity
    )
    SELECT
        s.ProductName,
        s.SKU,
        s.Price,
        s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Products p
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Delete removed products
    -------------------------------------------------
    DELETE FROM dbo.Products p
    USING dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    WHERE p.SKU = s.SKU
        AND s.SKU IS NULL;

    -- Note: The above DELETE logic appears incorrect in the original.
    -- It will never match rows because s.SKU IS NULL contradicts the join.
    -- Correct version (commented):
    -- DELETE FROM dbo.Products p
    -- WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    --     SELECT 1 FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    --     WHERE s.SKU = p.SKU
    -- );

END;
$$;
assumptions: Schema 'dbo' exists in PostgreSQL database or will be created
Tables 'Products' and 'ProductImportStaging' exist with compatible column types
ProductID is the primary key column in Products table
SKU column exists in both tables and is used for matching
No explicit transaction control needed as PostgreSQL procedures run in transaction context by default
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't return row counts by default in procedures)
The DELETE logic in the original appears to have a logical error (LEFT JOIN with WHERE s.SKU IS NULL will never match the join condition)

reviewFlags.reason: The original SQL Server DELETE logic appears incorrect. A LEFT JOIN with WHERE s.SKU IS NULL should identify products NOT in staging, but the join condition p.SKU = s.SKU combined with s.SKU IS NULL creates a contradiction. Review the intended business logic and consider using NOT EXISTS or WHERE p.SKU NOT IN (SELECT SKU FROM ProductImportStaging) instead.

compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL procedures automatically run in a transaction context. The explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION/COMMIT TRANSACTION from SQL Server is not needed and has been removed. If explicit transaction control is required, use COMMIT/ROLLBACK statements within the procedure.
PostgreSQL does not have an equivalent to SET NOCOUNT ON. PostgreSQL procedures do not return row counts to the client by default, so this behavior is already the default.
SQL Server UPDATE...FROM syntax converted to PostgreSQL UPDATE...FROM syntax. The table alias in SET clause is removed as PostgreSQL requires the actual table name in the SET clause.
SQL Server DELETE with FROM and JOIN converted to PostgreSQL DELETE...USING syntax. Note that the original logic may be flawed.
The 'dbo' schema is SQL Server convention. PostgreSQL uses 'public' by default. Ensure the 'dbo' schema exists or modify references accordingly.
